title: Low-Vision Dark Mode: Accessibility-focused token audit & component overrides
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a conservative, brand-safe token mapping and component override set that improves legibility for low-vision users in dark mode without breaking existing brand palettes or chart semantics. Scope covers tokens (surface/ink/interactive), button states, table row/stripe patterns, chart strokes and fills, and icon stroke inversion. Deliverables: (1) token mapping table with delta rules, (2) Figma component overrides and variants, (3) engineering token migration guide and token-lint rules, (4) QA checklist for low-vision testing.

Context: Current dark-mode variants rely on simple luminance inversion and brand anchors which can produce insufficient contrast for users with visual impairment, especially on dense tabular data and small interactive controls. We need a targeted variant set that is conservative (prefers increased contrast and preserved hue relationships) and can be toggled per-brand at the console level.

Key proposals: 
- Introduce a new token namespace: "lowVision.*" (e.g., lowVision.surfaceElevated, lowVision.inkPrimary, lowVision.brandAccentMuted) that layers on top of dark tokens when the accessibility toggle is enabled.
- Add algorithmic desaturation for brand accents above a configurable threshold so that accent hues remain identifiable but meet WCAG AA/AAA thresholds in context.
- For tables: prefer semi-opaque stripe overlays using background-blend tokens to preserve chart readability; provide an alternate high-contrast border token for table cells with focused/hover state.
- Buttons: enlarge focus outline and increase active/hover contrast while preserving silhouette; introduce a minimum interactive size recommendation for low-vision mode.
- Icons: adopt a stroke-recolor strategy that keeps stroke widths but switches to inkPrimary on dark surfaces; provide an alternate filled variant for critical affordances.
- Charts: map low-intensity area fills to reduced saturation + increased luminance delta; keep categorical hues distinct by enforcing minimum delta of 22 L* in perceptual space.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Token mapping doc published in Confluence and linked from component READMEs.
- Automated token-lint rule flags any new dark-mode token that doesn't satisfy the low-vision contrast matrix.
- Figma component kit contains a low-vision theme toggle and annotated variants for buttons, tables, icons, and charts.
- End-to-end QA: 3 representative console screens meet WCAG AA for 18pt text and AA for 14pt text with enhanced tokens, validated via color-contrast tools and manual low-vision simulator checks.

Constraints and trade-offs: 
- We cannot change customer-configurable brand colors; we must provide brand-safe fallbacks and clear guidance for when brand choices will be downgraded by the platform.
- Aggressive desaturation reduces brand distinctiveness; preference is given to legibility with an opt-in toggle for brand-preserving mode.

Migration notes for engineering: 
- Provide a mapping JSON that merges into existing token resolution at runtime: if lowVision.enabled => override tokens in order of specificity (component overrides -> control-level tokens -> global tokens).
- Add a runtime flag checked at initialization to avoid extra repaint costs for non-enabled customers.

Risks: 
- Edge cases where chart semantics rely on hue alone; mitigation: keep a chart-legend accent mapping that is exempt and provide textual labels by default in low-vision mode.

Next steps: 
1) Design draft in Figma (Marta) -> 2026-03-10 (done)
2) Engineering sync to review token merge strategy (schedule 2026-03-17)
3) Implement token-lint (ENG) and land small prototype behind feature flag (2026-03-24)

Related artefacts are in attachments.
